_comment: The brief wants three things on each document page: the final file, a revision narrative with evidence of process, and peer feedback. The last two are empty here on purpose, so those sections stay hidden — fill any of them in and the section comes back by itself. A draft of the CV revision narrative is parked in REVISION-DRAFTS.md.
title: Curriculum Vitae
description: Education, activities, and achievements on one page.
summary: A one-page CV aimed at marketing internships. It leads with my degree and the activities where I actually did marketing work, then condenses my academic awards, so an employer reads what I can do before they read what I have won.

title: Cover Letter
description: A tailored introduction for the roles I am applying to.
summary: A cover letter written for a specific marketing internship rather than a generic template, so it can show how I connect my coursework to what an employer actually asked for.
revision_narrative:
PLACEHOLDER — replace with your own account.

Explain how the letter started and how it ended up. Cover letters usually improve by getting more specific: naming the organisation, referencing something real about it, and cutting sentences that could appear in anyone's letter.

Say what you removed and why it was not doing any work.

process_evidence.label: Draft 1
process_evidence.note: PLACEHOLDER — the first attempt and what was generic about it.

process_evidence.label: Final
process_evidence.note: PLACEHOLDER — what made the final version specific.

peer_feedback.comment: PLACEHOLDER — what your reviewer said about the letter.
peer_feedback.response: PLACEHOLDER — what you changed as a result.

title: LinkedIn Profile
description: My professional profile and how it developed.
summary: A snapshot of my LinkedIn profile, included because it is the version of my professional self that an employer is most likely to find first — and the one that has to work without me in the room.
revision_narrative:
PLACEHOLDER — replace with your own account.

Describe how your headline and About section changed. A common improvement is moving from a job title to a statement of what you do and what you are looking for.

Mention anything you added — projects, coursework, skills — and why you judged it worth including.

process_evidence.label: Before
process_evidence.note: PLACEHOLDER — what the profile looked like at the start. A screenshot works well as evidence here.

process_evidence.label: After
process_evidence.note: PLACEHOLDER — the revised profile and what changed.
